evals.name: privilege-boundary-not-interactive-wizard
evals.prompt: The operator has to run the machine configuration elevated. Every step is scriptable. Write the script I will launch. Do not walk me through clicks.
evals.expected_output: The skill uses /wizard:unattended, not /wizard:generate. It copies template.ps1, leaves the library above # STAGES unchanged, and writes the procedure in the -Stages block of the Invoke-UnattendedRun call below # STAGES, with Assert-Elevation -Mode Required and no per-step confirmation. It prints the # STAGES block for approval, names the result-latest.json path (cutover.result/1) the agent will read back, and does not launch the real run; it runs `-Test` only after the human approves the block.
expectations: Chooses unattended rather than the interactive generate wizard
Authors PowerShell from template.ps1 without editing the library above # STAGES
Demands elevation with Assert-Elevation -Mode Required
Names the result-latest.json path the agent will read back
Does not launch the real run

evals.name: wsl-restart-runs-on-windows-host
evals.prompt: Write the unattended script that shuts down and restarts my WSL distro Ubuntu, then unregisters the old distro OldUbuntu.
evals.expected_output: The skill emits PowerShell to run on the Windows host, not a script inside the distro, and guards it with Assert-NotInside -Name Ubuntu. The unregister step is wrapped in Confirm-Irreversible, so the human types the name before it runs; the rest of the script stays unattended.
expectations: Emits PowerShell for the Windows host rather than a script run inside the distro
Guards the run with Assert-NotInside naming the distro
Wraps wsl --unregister in Confirm-Irreversible
Does not add per-step prompts to the non-irreversible steps

evals.name: dashboard-stays-on-generate
evals.prompt: I have to click through the Stripe dashboard and paste an API key. Build me the unattended script.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses the unattended shape for a dashboard click and routes to /wizard:generate, because a human is the actor, not only the privilege boundary.
expectations: Does not emit an unattended script for a dashboard click
Routes that procedure to /wizard:generate

evals.name: failed-proof-keeps-resource-held
evals.prompt: Write the unattended script that drains the build pool, restarts the agent host, and puts the pool back. Drain requests can exit nonzero even when the drain worked, and the check I have returns false while pools are still active.
evals.expected_output: The script uses Use-GuardedResource with a Prove block that throws or emits a truthy value; a Prove that returns $false keeps the resource held and Release never runs. The drain is proven with Wait-ForState polling the outcome (an assertion of a non-empty observation plus none active), not the exit code of the drain request, and -TolerateTakeExit is used because the request can exit nonzero.
expectations: Wraps the drain in Use-GuardedResource with Take, Prove and Release blocks
States that a Prove result of false, no output or a nonzero native exit keeps the resource held and skips Release
Proves the state with Wait-ForState polling the outcome rather than trusting the exit code of the request
Makes the Wait-ForState predicate assert a non-empty observation so an empty listing cannot pass
Does not launch the real run

evals.name: wsl-list-parse-is-guarded
evals.prompt: Write the unattended script that unregisters the WSL distro Ubuntu-26.04 only if it exists. Skip it when the distro is already gone.
evals.expected_output: The script reads the distro listing through Invoke-NativeUtf8 (wsl.exe writes UTF-16 otherwise) and passes the parsed names through Assert-ParsedState before any -Done guard, so an empty or failed read stops the run instead of reading as already absent. The unregister is declared with -Irreversible 'wsl --unregister Ubuntu-26.04', runs last, and sits behind Confirm-Irreversible. It re-verifies the distro is gone with Wait-ForState afterwards.
expectations: Wraps the wsl.exe listing in Invoke-NativeUtf8
Passes the parsed listing through Assert-ParsedState before the -Done guard
Declares the unregister in -Irreversible on Invoke-UnattendedRun
Places the destructive step last behind Confirm-Irreversible
Re-verifies the outcome with Wait-ForState after the destructive step

evals.name: preview-the-run-with-whatif-and-test
evals.prompt: Before I launch the elevated cutover script, I want to see what it would do without changing anything. How do I preview it, and can you check it yourself?
evals.expected_output: The skill tells the human to run the script with -WhatIf first and read its narration and blast radius counts, then make the real launch. After the human approves the # STAGES block, the agent's own safe entry is pwsh -File <script> -Test (safe only when every effect sits inside a helper's block), which reports the delta in result-dry-latest.json and invokes no mutating block. It notes the agent never launches the real run and that a dry run checks the plan and prerequisites, not that a state is reached.
expectations: Tells the human to run -WhatIf first and read the narration and blast radius
Names -Test as the agent-safe entry and reads result-dry-latest.json
Does not launch the real run
States that a dry run does not prove the target state is reached
